messages.subject: Modified Robust Design in JAGS?
parts:
Hi all,

I am a bit stuck at the moment and was hoping for a little feedback.  I have been trying to take Bailey's modified robust design (2004) fit originally with a modified version of MSSURVIV and get it to work in JAGS by extending the state-space multistate model in Kery and Schaub (2012).

I am working with a photo capture recapture vernal pool salamander dataset where multiple pools were drift fenced and salamanders were captured (photo taken), released inside the pool to breed and then captured again (photo taken) leaving the pool (if they didn't die breeding).  The dataset also contains a count of the number of metamorphs emerging from each pool the following spring.  So, I have a fecundity rate or average metamoprhs per female if I can control for detection and perhaps survival at the pool.  

Detection is fairly high with few individuals getting past the drift fence without being captured but prior to matching the 14,000 photos I ended up screening some photos which had significant distortion due to photo glare.  I used Amphident, a photo matching software that converts photos to a coarsened red/black image which allows you to see how distorted an image is due to photo glare.  So, detection for me is potentially a bit lower especially in earlier years of the study when photo quality was not great.  

The model is a bit complicated due to the fact that females "skip" breeding so you have a multi state model with an observable and unobservable state.   You also have two different intervals.  This includes a breeding interval between those secondary occasions when some subset of the females are at the pool breeding and a non-breeding interval when all individuals are in the surrounding upland forest.  

Since you have no information on individuals in the unobservable state you have to constrain survival of unobservable individuals to be the same as individuals in the observable state during the non-breeding period.  Also, individuals can transition between states only during the non-breeding interval. 

Other issues are differing interval lengths by year/pool due to females brooding eggs until a pool fills with water which differs year to year and pool to pool.   

Right now I think I am simulating data that mimic my real data, but when I fit the models in JAGS the estimates of survival and state transition are biased.   

I potentially have just made a mistake or two in my state transition or detection matrices or perhaps this state-space format JAGS is not feasible.   I would be grateful to anyone providing some advice to help me move forward.  I think the model would be applicable to herp data such as mine and beyond.  

I attached my current code for simulating capture histories and fitting the JAGS model.  

best,
Kris
